purpose: Independent review of one effect's filmstrip. The reviewer is not the author: it gets the strip image(s), the manifest entry (id, category, element, duration, peak, impact, design) and this rubric, but not the recipe code, so it judges what is on screen rather than what was intended.

scale.1: present but weak; a player would not notice it
scale.3: reads instantly and has a distinct identity

criteria.question: From the first lit tile alone, can you tell what the effect is (hit, slash, element, buff...)?
Is there anticipation -> contact -> body -> secondary -> dissipation (or the slow fade-in / inward build for heals, buffs and charges)? Is the contact the brightest moment and only 2-5 frames long?
criteria.look_at: tile frame labels against manifest peak

criteria.question: At the strongest tile, is there a white-hot core, a saturated body and a darker rim or residue, rather than one flat colour?
criteria.look_at: peak tile; bright-background strip if provided

criteria.question: Does the main shape erode, sweep, or distort over time, or does it only scale and fade like a sticker?
criteria.look_at: the main shape across consecutive tiles

criteria.question: Do secondary particles burst fast and then slow down, and move the way the element should (fire up, ice falls, dark draws in, holy descends or rises)?
Do arcs, columns and ground decals sit on or under the dummy rather than beside it or floating?
Does the last third still show deliberate dissipation, or is it empty or cut off?
Would this be distinguishable from other effects of the same category if it were recoloured grey?
criteria.look_at: whole strip; overview pages for siblings

schema.worst: criterion id with the lowest score
schema.fix: one concrete change for the worst criterion, in recipe terms (layer, timing, texture, motion)

rules: Score only what is visible; do not trust the design note.
verdict is iterate when any score is below 2.
Name one fix only: each iteration round changes one class of problem.
